title: Why Venus Melts Lead: The Cloud Physics You Missed (2026)
description:
Most people think Mercury is the hottest planet because it's closest to the Sun. They're wrong. Venus is 465°C. Why? It's not the distance. It's the clouds.

In this 60-second breakdown, we look at the specific physics of Venus' sulfuric acid atmosphere. We show you how the thick CO2 layer traps infrared radiation, creating a surface hot enough to melt lead. No fluff. Just the mechanism.

Watch to the end to see what those white clouds are actually made of. It's not water.

#Venus #SpaceScience #GreenhouseEffect #Astronomy #Physics
